content.text:
# create published an empty `latest` and broke `fa update`; the
          # binaries job owns creation, draft-first). The tag push rides
          # the checkout App token above (gh-1172).
        run: bash scripts/auto_release.sh

  # PR-gate twin of the release `binaries` job: the CLI bundle must compile
  # on every supported platform and actually run (`fa --help`) BEFORE a PR
  # can merge — but only when the CLI surface could have changed (issue
  # #177: a docs/app PR must not pay for five platform builds).
  #
  # gh-1280: merge-blocking validations ride `workflow_dispatch` (Machine SM
  # dispatches this workflow on the PR head; the dispatched run registers its
  # check runs on the head SHA), while this gate fired only on `pull_request`
  # events. Every real validation run therefore skipped the matrix and the
  # required "Binaries smoke gate" context went green-by-skip — a broken arch
  # build (the v1.0.512 linux/arm64 class) could never block a merge. On a
  # dispatched run the classifier treats everything as affected (non-PR
  # filter arm), so the full matrix runs exactly when validation is due;
  # docs-only pull_request runs keep the #177 path skip.

  binaries-pr:
    name: Binaries (PR)
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    timeout-minutes: 30
    needs: changes
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch') &&
      (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - runner: windows-latest
            os: windows
            arch: x64
          - runner: macos-latest
            os: macos
            arch: arm64
          - runner: macos-15-intel
            os: macos
            arch: x64
          - runner: ubuntu-latest
            os: linux
            arch: x64
          - runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            os: linux
            arch: arm64
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: Build CLI bundle
        shell: bash
        run: |
          # Same bundle layout as the release job: bundle/bin/fa (+ lib/).
          dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=build/out
          if [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = "windows" ]; then
            mv build/out/bundle/bin/fah.exe build/out/bundle/bin/fa.exe
          else
            mv build/out/bundle/bin/fah build/out/bundle/bin/fa
            chmod +x build/out/bundle/bin/fa
          fi
          # gh-1522: the committed pubspec is the 0.0.0-dev placeholder —
          # stamp the PR bundle's version.txt from git describe (short sha
          # on shallow checkouts) so `fa --version` stays meaningful.
          version=$(git describe --tags --always --dirty 2>/dev/null || echo 0.0.0-dev)
          version="${version#v}"
          echo "$version" > build/out/bundle/version.txt

      - name: Ad-hoc sign CLI binary (macOS)
        if: matrix.os == 'macos'
        shell: bash
        run: codesign --force --sign - build/out/bundle/bin/fa

      - name: Smoke — the binary runs (fa --help)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa"
          [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = "windows" ] && bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa.exe"
          out=$("$bin" --help)
          echo "$out"
          [ -n "$out" ] || { echo "fa --help produced no output"; exit 1; }

  # Aggregation job so branch protection can require ONE stable context
  # ("Binaries smoke gate") instead of five matrix-leg names.
  binaries-smoke-gate:
    name: Binaries smoke gate
    needs: binaries-pr
    # gh-1280: same event fix as binaries-pr — on the SM validation
    # dispatches this aggregate must RUN (and carry a real conclusion),
    # never satisfy the required context by skipping.
    if: always() && (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: All platforms built and smoked
        if: needs.binaries-pr.result == 'success' || needs.binaries-pr.result == 'skipped'
        run: echo "binaries-pr = ${{ needs.binaries-pr.result }}"
      - name: Fail the gate
        if: needs.binaries-pr.result != 'success' && needs.binaries-pr.result != 'skipped'
        run: |
          echo "binaries-pr result: ${{ needs.binaries-pr.result }}"
          exit 1

  # Every failing TAG run must reach a human-facing tracker item the
  # moment it goes red (user ask 2026-09-17): PR-dispatch failures are
  # visible on the PR itself, and gh-1537 retired the post-merge main CI
  # run — so the only `push` events this workflow ever receives are v*
  # tag pushes (release flow), whose reds used to live only in the Actions
  # tab. Files/updates one issue per red run, always assigned to
  # ai-teammate. quality-gate aggregates every leg (always()), so its
  # failure verdict covers the whole matrix — the fa#456 lesson on
  # transitive skips: this job keys on the aggregator's result directly.
  ci-red-report:
    name: CI red → issue (ai-teammate)
    needs: [quality-gate]
    if: ${{ always() && github.event_name == 'push' && needs.quality-gate.result == 'failure' }}
    permissions:
      issues: write
      contents: read
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: File or update the red-run issue
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          failed=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" \
            --jq '[.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "failure") | .name] | join(", ")')
          title="[ci-red] $REF failed"
          url="https://github.com/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID"
          body="**Failed jobs:** ${failed:-unknown}
          **Run:** $url

          Auto-filed by the ci-red-report leg; assignee ai-teammate. Closes manually when the ref goes green."
          existing=$(gh issue list --repo "$REPO" --state open --label ci-red \
            --json number --jq ".[0].number // empty")
          if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
            gh issue comment "$existing" --repo "$REPO" --body "$body"
            echo "commented on #$existing"

# Machine SM — thin stub over the dmtools-agents factory (reusable pack).
#
# The whole reconcile tick (engine checkout, dmtools install, rule run)
# lives in IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml. This
# file carries only the triggers (cron + manual dry dispatch) and the
# call. NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm`
# group — a caller declaring the same group deadlocks the called workflow
# (it waits forever on a group its own caller holds).

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true


# The factory's own permissions block cannot raise rights above the
# caller, and the org default caps the token at read-only — the silent
# update-branch path (workflow token, updatePullRequestBranch) failed
# live with "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update
# this pull request" until this explicit block lifted the ceiling.
permissions:
  # contents: write — update-branch pushes a merge commit onto the PR head
  # branch; PullRequests: write alone is denied at the refs level (live:
  # "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update this pull
  # request" even with PullRequests: write granted).
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge

--signal)
      if [ "$#" -ge 2 ]; then sig="$2"; shift 2
      else exec "$FA_REAL_PKILL" "$@"; fi
      ;;
    --signal=*) sig="${1#--signal=}"; shift ;;
    --) fa_dd=1; shift; break ;;
    -[0-9]*) sig="$1"; shift ;;
    -[Ss][Ii][Gg][A-Za-z]*|-[A-Z][A-Z]*) sig="$1"; shift ;;
    # Value-taking selection flags (procps: -u -U -g -s -t -P -G -r -O -q
    # -F): the value may ride the next argv item (split form, e.g.
    # `pkill -u "$(id -u)" -f <pat>`). Consume both into the selection so
    # the guarded path still runs — execing the real, unshimed pkill here
    # would leave the harness unprotected (the gh-1763 crash shape). The
    # glued forms (-urot) ride the generic case below.
    -u|-U|-g|-s|-t|-P|-G|-r|-O|-q|-F)
      if [ "$#" -ge 2 ]; then
        sel="$sel $1 $2"
        shift 2
      else
        exec "$FA_REAL_PKILL" "$@"
      fi
      ;;
    -*) sel="$sel $1"; shift ;;
    *) break ;;
  esac
done
# Exactly one operand (the pattern) must remain; anything else — unknown
# flags interleaved with it, extra operands — is the real pkill's call.
if [ "$#" -ne 1 ]; then
  if [ "$fa_dd" = 1 ]; then exec "$FA_REAL_PKILL" -- "$@"; fi
  exec "$FA_REAL_PKILL" "$@"
fi

# The selection flags ride along: pgrep shares pkill's selection engine.

# Issue #675: the suite must be immune to a hostile ambient env — the
  # dmtools ai-teammate runner exports FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG /
  # FAH_PROVIDER, which used to decide test fate through the args resolver.
  # Run the non-integration suite under the same hostile env so any
  # ambient-env read that leaks back into resolution regresses loudly.
  # gh-1198 rework: the runner now ALSO exports FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE (the
  # provider-queue env won over the file queue and silently flipped the
  # /providers queue editor tests to the env-wins refusal on the PR head) —
  # the var rides the same hostile block so a future ambient read of it
  # regresses here, not only on the runner.
  hostile-env:
    name: Hostile ambient env
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai
      FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: '{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnvVar":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}'
      FAH_PROVIDER: zai
      FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE: '[{"provider_type":"zai","provider_config":{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnv":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}}]'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: dart test under hostile ambient env
        run: dart test --exclude-tags integration

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Nightly parity (2026-09-23): the two legs that stayed nightly-only went
  # red on main night after night before anyone looked — the CLI-coverage
  # ratchet (12.07% < 12.17%) and the Terminal-visual PTY suite (five
  # regressions, several cascading out of fixed-port collisions). Both legs
  # are part of the COMMON PR suite: they run on every CI invocation (the
  # Machine SM dispatches ci.yml per PR head), unconditioned by path — a
  # diff that breaks them must red-block THE PR, never the 3:30 nightly.
  # gh-1538: nightly is builds + integration-only now — this PR leg IS the
  # only Terminal-visual run (the nightly cli-visual duplicate is retired).
  # gh-1537 retired the post-merge main CI run, so this pre-merge leg is
  # the only Terminal-visual gate any tree ever sees; nightly's remaining
  # legs are a scheduled backstop, not a second merge gate.
  # gh-1300 (2026-10-06): the PTY/CLI shards pay toolchain+boot ONCE per
  # run, not per test. Every integration test spawns a fresh CLI; JIT
  # `dart bin/fah.dart` cost VM start + CFE kernel compile ~30 s PER SPAWN
  # on loaded ARM runners (the dominant term: 29 files, 3 shards x
  # ~350 s). This job compiles the AOT bundle once, the shards download
  # it and point the FA_BIN seam (test/integration/pty_harness.dart,
  # faCliCommand) at it — spawn ~1 s, per-test isolation untouched (each
  # spawn is still a fresh process with its own env/cwd). The binary MUST
  # match the PR's sources: built fresh in this run, never cached across
  # runs; the shards fail loudly if it is missing or dead (`test -x` +
  # `--version` smoke), never silently fall back to JIT.
  fa-aot-build:
    name: AOT fa binary (compiled once per run, gh-1300)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      # Same hooks cache key as the shards: the build pays the native
      # assets hooks here so the shard-side restore is warm.
      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-
      - run: dart pub get
      - name: dart build cli (AOT bundle, same shape install_local.sh ships)
        run: |
          dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=fa-local
          # The installer writes version.txt into the bundle; mirror it so
          # `fa --version` from the AOT binary reports the real version
          # (the _packageVersion() fallback chain reads bundle/version.txt).
          # gh-1522: the committed pubspec is the 0.0.0-dev placeholder —
          # PR runs stamp from git describe (falls back to the short sha
          # on shallow checkouts); release runs get the exact tag from the
          # release binaries job.
          version=$(git describe --tags --always --dirty 2>/dev/null || echo 0.0.0-dev)
          version="${version#v}"

  prelude function, both excluding the harness pid chain + process group

  rejects — exec the real, unshimed binary and are NOT covered by the

- name: Quality gates (broken goldens + Type-2 duplication, issue 1106)
        # gh-1738: + docs/app — the similarity gate scans the whole tree
        # (docs/, prompts/, flutter_app/, packages/ included); no project
        # pub get needed (global tool, config+file gates only).
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.docs == 'true'
        run: dart pub global run crap4dart check --baseline

      # Issue #1234 rework: 0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override (a
      # gates.loc.sources key is a ConfigException — caught here on
      # 019ede65), and the package config's sources drive the CRAP census
      # too, so test/ + example/ get the SAME loc gate from the companion
      # config (crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml) — the scope the retired shell
      # guards (gh-1232) scanned there. No baseline: nothing exceeds 2800
      # today, and the ceiling itself is the point.
      - name: Loc scope gate (test/ + example/, gh-1232 whole-tree ceiling)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart pub global run crap4dart check --config crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml --only loc

      - name: Duplication guard (lib/ < 1%)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          npx --yes jscpd@5 --min-tokens 50 --min-lines 5 --reporters json \
            --output /tmp/jscpd-ci lib/ || true
          python3 - <<'EOF'
          import json, sys
          try:
              with open('/tmp/jscpd-ci/jscpd-report.json') as f:
                  pct = json.load(f)['statistics']['total']['percentage']
          except Exception:
              pct = 0.0
          print(f'Duplication: {pct}% (threshold < 1.0%)')
          sys.exit(0 if float(pct) < 1.0 else 1)
          EOF

      # Issue #487: cross-module duplication gate (issue body measured 20
      # files shipped as app↔core/fa_ui/browser_ext clones). Runs the SAME
      # stage the pre-commit hook runs — one marker, parity diffable. The
      # app leg matters: most cross-module clones are born on the app side
      # and the CRAP/dup steps above stay core/shared-scoped.
      - name: Cross-module duplication ratchet (issue #487)

# PR #1942 rework — validation red root-caused and fixed (test fixture)

## Issues/Notes

- **Open review threads: 0** — `pr_discussions_raw.json` census lists no open threads
  (`{"threads": []}`), so `outputs/review_replies.json` is `{"replies": []}` (nothing to
  answer; the single general bot comment is the arming boilerplate, not a review thread).
- **`ci_failures.md` has no "Violations you must fix (N owned)" table** — the failure data
  was three check contexts with 404 logs. Root cause recovered from the live run data
  (validation run [`40690203051`](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/40690203051),
  dispatched on this head by Machine SM):
  - The three red contexts (`Quality gate`, `JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)`,
    `Binaries smoke gate`) are the SM's bridge-free validation **stamps** (zero-duration,
    no steps, created 13:04:25Z via the checks API), not independent leg failures. They
    mirror attempt 1's aggregate verdict.
  - The only real red leg in attempt 1 **and** attempt 2 (re-dispatched by the watchdog,
    both times `12849 tests passed, 1 failed, 12 skipped`) is **Hostile ambient env**:
    `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` →
    `AC2d (gh-1763) killall --signal TERM reaps its victim (unique comm name)` expecting
    `rc=0`, actual `rc=1` (line 515 in the attempt-1 tree). The aggregate `Quality gate`
    failed solely because of it; `JS engine integration` was **skipped** (gated on
    quality-gate); all five `Binaries (PR)` matrix legs and the smoke gate were **green**.
  - This PR's diff (`flutter_app/**` + `CHANGELOG.md`) cannot influence that leg — it is a
    pure-Dart CLI suite (`dart test --exclude-tags integration`, flutter_app not even
    pub-resolved there). The red is a **runner-image regression**, now proven
    **deterministic**: the `ubuntu-latest` image ships **uutils-coreutils** as
    `/usr/bin/sleep`; uutils is a multi-call binary that dispatches on `argv[0]`, so the
    test's victim fixture — a *renamed copy* of the sleep binary (`fa_kl_271`) — dies
    instantly with ``coreutils: unknown program 'fa_kl_271'`` (exit 1). The later
    `killall` therefore finds no live victim, `pgrep -x` misses, the shim honestly exits 1.
    Reproduced locally byte-identical to the CI failure before the fix; green 16/16 runs
    after it. Red is now 2/3 on this head, so this push also provides the NEW head the
    owner directive (2026-10-04) requires.

## Approach

- TDD: **RED** — ran `dart test test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart --plain-name
  "killall --signal TERM reaps its victim (unique comm name)"` on the unfixed tree:
  `Expected: 'rc=0' / Actual: 'rc=1'` — the exact CI failure, local and deterministic.
- **GREEN** — two-part test-fixture fix (no production code changed; `rc=1` is legitimate
  killall semantics for "no match", so the shims stay untouched):
  1. The killall victim fixture now copies `/bin/sh` (resolved via `command -v sh`)
     instead of the sleep binary and starts it as `<tmp>/fa_kl_271 -c 'read _'`.
     `dash`/`bash` are argv0-agnostic (no multi-call dispatch), and `read _` blocks on
     the never-written stdin pipe — the same long-lived, unique-comm victim `sleep 271`
     used to provide, on every host that passes the existing `hostHasPgrep` skip.
  2. New `waitUntilPgrepMatches()` helper (mirrors the suite's `stillAlive()`
     load-independence pattern): polls `pgrep` — the exact matcher both shims delegate
     to — until it lists the victim pid (~5s budget), before the killer runs. This closes
     the fork→exec visibility race in all three AC2d reap tests (killall: `pgrep -x`,
     the two `pkill -f` siblings: `pgrep -f "sleep 271"`), where a loaded runner could
     otherwise produce an honest `rc=1`.
- No CHANGELOG entry: the fix is CI/test infrastructure, no user-facing behavior change.

## Files Modified

- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` — victim fixture (`/bin/sh` copy + `-c 'read _'`
  instead of a renamed sleep copy), new `waitUntilPgrepMatches()` helper, visibility wait
  in the three AC2d reap tests (+42/−9).

## Test Coverage

- RED proof (pre-fix, local): the named killall test failed with the CI signature
  (`rc=1` at the `expect` on the killall result).
- Post-fix:
  - `dart test test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` → **26/26 passed**.
  - The previously failing test alone re-run **15×** → 0 failures.
  - Full `test/env/` suite under the leg's exact hostile env vars
    (`FA_PROVIDER_TYPE`/`FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`) →
    **151/151 passed**.
  - Full hostile-env leg command `dart test --exclude-tags integration` (the exact
    `hostile-env` job step) run locally on the fixed tree — result recorded in the run
    log of this rework pass.
  - `dart analyze test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` → no issues;
    `dart format --set-exit-if-changed` → clean.
- Gate-safety audit for the whole-tree checks this push re-triggers: the CRAP census
  scope is `[lib, bin]` (test/ only joins the ≤2800-line loc-scope ceiling — file is
  696 lines), the jscpd duplication gate scans `lib/` only, and flutter_app gates are
  untouched by this diff.

## Summary

**PR #1942 rework** — 0 open review threads; the rework trigger was a red validation head.

**Root cause (from live run data, since `ci_failures.md` logs were 404s):** the three red contexts (`Quality gate`, `JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)`, `Binaries smoke gate`) are the Machine-SM's bridge-free validation **stamps** (zero-duration, API-created), mirroring validation run 40690203051's aggregate verdict. The only real red — in **both** attempts (watchdog re-ran attempt 2, same `12849 passed / 1 failed`) — was the `Hostile ambient env` leg: `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` → `killall --signal TERM reaps its victim (unique comm name)` (`rc=1`); aggregate log states verbatim `Quality gate FAILED: a leg is failure (hostile-env)`.

**Why:** the `ubuntu-latest` image rolled **uutils-coreutils** as `/usr/bin/sleep` — a multi-call binary dispatching on `argv[0]`, so the test's victim (a *renamed copy* of sleep) dies instantly with `coreutils: unknown program 'fa_kl_271'`; the later `killall` finds no live victim. Deterministic on new images, unrelated to this PR's `flutter_app` diff — the exact scenario the no-owned-table branch prescribes as "fix CI root cause: test setup".

**Fix (TDD, test-only):** RED reproduced locally byte-identical (`Expected 'rc=0' / Actual 'rc=1'`); GREEN = victim fixture now copies `/bin/sh` (argv0-agnostic) started as `fa_kl_271 -c 'read _'` (blocks on the never-written stdin pipe), plus a new `waitUntilPgrepMatches()` helper (mirrors the suite's `stillAlive()` load-independence pattern) closing the fork→exec visibility race in all three AC2d reap tests. Post-fix: file 26/26, ×15 repeats green, `test/env/` 151/151 under the leg's exact hostile env, and the **full leg command `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: 12850 passed / 12 skipped / 0 failed, exit 0**.

**Push:** head `1c07687f99` on `feat/private-network-account-discovery` (tree byte-identical to the verified fix; a harness WIP auto-save trail carries it — force-with-lease was denied, so the fast-forwarded remote head with identical content was kept). Validation run `40698995971` is queued on the new head.
